one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-01) almost certainly contains Q3 2026 results. The date is not yet announced (no 8-K or release on EDGAR as of 2026-10-02), but the last four reports came on Mondays in the last week of the first month of the quarter, so Oct 26-29 is likely. The Q3 guide (revenue $210-216M, product $110-116M, royalties $69-75M, non-GAAP EPS $0.75-0.82) is achievable, and the royalty step-down is lumpiness after an elevated Q2. The stock will trade on the Q4 product guide and 2027 RDIMM/MRDIMM commentary. Round 1 had two errors here. First, the Q2 print drew a -9% next-day move, not a positive one. Second, the ASR 8-K says the $100M ASR was expected to complete by the end of Q3 2026, so its bid is over. Both lead me to remove my small upward drift. The last four prints all fell 9-21% the next day, and the stock is +39% in three weeks from the $80.39 Sep-14 close, so expectations are higher going into this print. Four prints is a small sample and I have no view on the actual numbers, so I tilt only modestly: a lognormal centred at ~$110.5 (about -1.3%) with a 20% one-month sigma, slightly above 80%/3.5 because of the earnings event.

fair_value.method: Forward P/E: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 is ~$3.98 (0.25 x FY27 $3.58 + 0.75 x FY28 $4.12) x 29x = $115. FCF yield: horizon FCF ~$390M less ~$50M/yr of net-share-settlement taxes = $340M at 3.0%, plus ~$0.78B net cash, over ~108M shares = $112. Weighted 60/40, ~$114.

inputs_detail.derivation: Sum of Q1 and Q2 actuals, the Q3 guide midpoint and Q4E ~$0.84 (product growth continuing, royalties ~$70-75M). Matches the ~$3.04 2026 consensus the supervisor read on stockanalysis.

The Q3'26 guide annualizes to ~$3.15. Add ~15-17% product growth: MRDIMM material in 2027 per management, companion chips rising, and RDIMM unit growth of 12-15% (Baird) that can run above TrendForce's 15-20% bit-supply growth as modules shift to 32/64GB. Royalties ~flat. Up from $3.55 in round 1 because the bit-vs-unit point makes the unit cap less binding. The unverified $3.72 consensus (paywalled) is an upper anchor only.
~15% growth on 2027E, near the 2025-26 product growth rate (15-22%), with the buyback trimming the share count ~1%/yr.
The year starting Oct-2027 is ~1/4 FY27 + 3/4 FY28: 0.25 x 3.58 + 0.75 x 4.12 = $3.98. Round 1's $3.90 under-weighted FY28.

Today the stock is ~37x 2026E and ~31x 2027E. I assume de-rating to 29x NTM as growth decelerates, with the DOJ probe and the DRAM-supply debate still open, and with the market repeatedly selling the prints (4 of 4 next-day drops). That is 1 turn below round 1 for the reaction record and the higher NTM base. Analyst targets ($100-180, average ~$148) are evidence, not the answer.

At today's price, EV ~$11.3B on ~$285M 2026E FCF is ~2.5%. A 3.0% yield on the after-settlement-tax figure is modest de-rating, consistent with the P/E leg.

bear.story: 2027 RDIMM unit growth falls short of even the 12-15% Baird case as DRAM goes to HBM, MRDIMM slips beyond the Diamond Rapids/Venice ramps, royalties fade on a renewal, and/or the DOJ grand-jury matter escalates. 2027 EPS ~$3.1 at ~23x. Probability trimmed 1 point from round 1 because units can outgrow bits, so outright unit contraction is less likely.

base.story: Product revenue grows mid-teens in 2027 on RCD share plus PMIC/SPD/companion chips and early MRDIMM; royalties ~flat; buybacks continue; ~29x NTM EPS of ~$4.0-4.1.

bull.story: A strong AI-inference/agentic CPU server cycle in 2027 drives MRDIMM ($600-700M SAM) and SOCAMM2/LPDDR5X server module ramps; companion chips reach mid-teens % of product; EPS run-rate >$4.3 and the multiple back near 40x, retesting the $174 high. The lognormal for this branch is wide (sigma 38%) so P(>=2x) is ~7%, in line with the base rate for an 80%-vol name.

thesis_break_reason: A sustained close near or below $72 is ~7% under the $77.89 March 2026 low and ~18x NTM EPS of ~$4.0. The stock did not reach that level even through the -21% April print and the September low ($80.39 close). It would most likely mean something fundamental: a guided product-revenue decline (RDIMM units actually contracting, or RCD share loss to Montage/Renesas), a royalty renewal shortfall with a concentrated licensee (Customer A 22-29% of quarterly revenue), or a DOJ indictment or forced change to licensing practices.

reasoning: Round-2 revision. The supervisor's fact-checks corrected three things in my file, and I re-checked one primary fact myself. (1) The Q2 reaction was -9%, not positive, and all four of the last prints fell 9-21% the next day. (2) The ASR 8-K text (re-read from EDGAR) says completion was expected by the end of Q3 2026, so it is not a Q4 support catalyst. (3) My NTM weighting under-weighted FY28. The bit-vs-unit point (TrendForce's bit supply plus the 32/64GB module mix shift) makes outright RDIMM unit contraction less likely, so I nudged 2027E to $3.58 and the bear probability down a point. The 10-Q's $52.7M H1 of net-share-settlement taxes is a real SBC cash cost, so I now haircut FCF for it, which lowers the FCF leg from $118 to $112. The P/E leg moves from $117 to $115 (higher NTM EPS of $3.98 offset by 29x instead of 30x). The blended fair value is ~$114 (from $117), about 2% above spot, so the 12-month view is again mostly volatility around modest drift. I agree with the supervisor's fair value but derive it independently. My multiple is higher (29x vs 28x), my FCF leg is lower and I weight the two legs 60/40 rather than 75/25. Ladder: a mixture of bear $72 (24%, sigma 32%), base $118 (50%, sigma 27%) and bull $170 (26%, sigma 38%) gives a median of ~$116 and a mean of ~$127. I widened the right tail on the supervisor's base-rate feedback: P(>=224) goes from 4.6% to 7.3% and P(>=280) from 1.0% to 3.2%, consistent with a ~7% 20-year base rate for doubling in 12 months. I kept a small far-left floor for a DOJ/customer tail. The 1-month ladder is re-centred from $112.5 to $110.5 (ended ASR, +39% rally, reaction record), with a 20% sigma. Research limits: EDGAR shows no Q3-date announcement as of Oct 2, the Rambus IR page did not render, and call transcripts remained inaccessible, so management commentary still comes from Quartr summaries.
